description.p: Riviera is a parametric Building Information Modeling (BIM) application for architecture, structure and MEP. IFC is its native file format, so there is no proprietary container. Every operation can be driven by Lua scripts and by AI agents through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
This is an early pre-release. It already models a small building end to end:

ul.li: Straight and curved walls, doors and windows, floors, ceilings and decks
Hip, gable, arched and domed roofs with eaves and dormers
Stairs, railings with gates, rooms, levels and grids
Overlap detection with kept booleans, and door clearance checks
Plans, ceiling plans, sections, elevations, schedules and sheets to PDF and COBie

description.p: Help lists sample models to open, and the Castle Turret plugin shows what a Lua plugin can do.

description.p: Eleventh pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.11), for testing: the program is that of 0.1.0-pre.10. The Windows installer now removes what an install under the old spelling left behind when it upgrades one: the old programs, their Start menu and desktop shortcuts, and their .ifc association.

Tenth pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.10), for testing. The project's name is now spelled BIM Riviera; files, settings and property sets saved under the old spelling still open. Vertical transport: elevators sized under rule packs (passenger, hospital, freight, vehicle and small lifts, panoramic cars and glass hoistways) with their hoistways, landings, machine spaces, power estimates and schedule; escalators and moving walks, stairlifts and inclined platform lifts; elevator and escalator traffic checks; transit escalators and fare lines in stations. Egress: routes across levels by stairs, escalators and evacuation elevators, drawn in the plans, with their points typed or clicked; NFPA 130 platform clearing times, with occupant loads from trains and the standing area, escalators, evacuation elevators and the wait at fare lines. FileEngine wherever a file is read or written: exports, imports, Component Libraries with update notices, parameter libraries, scripts, keynotes and publish sets.

Ninth pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.9), for testing. The docked Issues pane lists every issue, open and resolved (greyed and marked), with a status filter and search, wherever the model's issues are kept: FileEngine, a project on a BCF API issue server such as OpenConstructionERP (preliminary), or the model itself. Issues are read whenever a FileEngine model opens, and replies, resolving, edits and new issues go back to the server; the model's own issues can be published to it. The FileEngine browser enters folders without closing its window.

Eighth pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.8), for testing. Product data field sets are published to FileEngine as extraction prompt sets, and the review opens the marked-up PDF with each value's evidence highlighted. IFC files get default colours that web viewers such as FileEngine's xeokit preview show: translucent windows and distinct walls and floors, also for models saved before default colours existed. Steam rooms place their steam generator and check its distance and the control's height. macOS builds are fixed.

Seventh pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.7), for testing: bathrooms. Rule packs for US, ADA and English codes with fixture clear spaces, grab bars and fixture counts; generic fixtures and accessories, and products to swap in; layouts from templates, toilet cores and locker rooms; electrical zones, shower falls and waterproofing; hot tubs, saunas (heater sized from the room, vents, sensor, door vent and notice), steam rooms and whirlpool baths, with ADA spa access; interior elevations and schedules, an HTML compliance report and BCF issues; and tile set-out on walls and floors. Also issues on FileEngine models, local material documents, and greenhouse heating pipes and pad-and-fan cooling.

Sixth pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.6), for testing: models on FileEngine (Proxima File Vault): connections and sign-in with an API credential, opening a model from a folder, saving new versions with Ctrl+S that stop if someone else saved first (save a copy beside it, overwrite, or open theirs read-only), and the version history, to open or restore any version. BIMserver gains history, compare and restore, a sync lock, conflicts decided one by one, and advisory ownership of the elements being edited. Also a performance profiler, and greenhouse screens, quick heat loss, ventilation, CO₂ enrichment and heating sizing.

Fifth pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.5), for testing: BIMserver projects (File › BIMserver…): servers and login, publishing a project, opening a server project as a working copy, checking in, and Get Latest and Synchronise, which merge other users' changes element by element and parameter by parameter and stop at conflicts for a choice. Greenhouses gain sawtooth ranges, frame systems, side and gable vents, roll-up sides, a headhouse, glazed vaults and domes, geodesic domes, high-wire gutters, growing layouts in rooms, crop climates, crop light by month and grow lights. The Flatpak may now use the network, for the servers the user adds.

Fourth pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.4), for testing: greenhouses (gable, gutter-connected multispan, Venlo, hoop and gothic tunnels) made by one Glazed Enclosure tool, with glass walls filling the gables, doors, ridge vents, gutters and a steel frame; saved Hide in View and graphic overrides; crop regions sized and dragged, and cropped to scope boxes in sections and elevations; typed section box and slice positions.

Third pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.3), for testing: spot elevations, coordinates and slopes, keynote tags and legends, legend views, crop regions with annotation crop (dragged, sized or following a scope box), and labels in 3D attached to their elements.

Second pre-release (tag 0.1.0-pre.2), for testing: structure, steel and concrete detailing, MEP systems, analysis, coordination (BCF issues), annotation in sections, elevations and 3D, and a sample with a walkthrough for every ribbon tab.
